units.summary: New test injects a late append via a hook between block write and eviction, then checks the series survives (isolation on) or is evicted (isolation off), before and after restart.
units.headline: Test: late append during compaction survives eviction and restart
units.reason: New test only; no production behavior change.

units.summary: New test opens an appender before compaction, commits it in the pre-evict hook, and verifies the series is retained and the sample survives restart.
units.headline: Test: pre-opened appender committing mid-compaction keeps series
units.reason: New test only.

units.summary: Adds a small predicate that reports whether a series has no OOO state. It is used as an eviction and filter predicate.
units.headline: Add isSeriesWithoutOOO predicate helper
units.reason: Trivial helper; its behavior is visible through the callers.

units.summary: Extracts the existing stale-NaN check (float, histogram and float histogram) into a helper, identical to the logic previously inlined in gcStaleSeries.
units.headline: Extract stale-series check into helper
units.reason: Obviously equivalent extraction of existing logic.

units.summary: truncateStaleSeries now delegates to truncateSeries. Eviction requires no OOO data, a stale last value, and no appendID above the watermark. This changes eviction semantics: series with OOO data are now skipped.
units.headline: Stale truncation adds OOO and appendID watermark guards
units.reason: Changes which series are evicted from the head and tombstoned in the WAL; data-loss-sensitive.
focus: The watermark is captured before the block write so that later commits are detected
Skipping series with OOO data does not leave them stuck forever
Callers pass the right watermark

units.summary: New eviction path for selected series. It evicts only series without OOO data and without samples committed after the watermark, via truncateSeries.
units.headline: New selected-series eviction with OOO and watermark guards
units.reason: Evicting head series and writing WAL tombstones is data-loss-sensitive.
focus: Predicate runs under the series lock (hasAppendIDAbove requires it)
Behavior when isolation is disabled: the guard is a no-op
Series skipped here are not tombstoned

units.summary: New helper iterates the series' isolation txs ring and reports whether any appendID exceeds the watermark. It returns false when isolation is disabled (txs nil).

issues.title: Watermark guard silently ineffective when isolation disabled
issues.failure_scenario: With isolation disabled, a sample committed between block write and eviction is not detected; the series is evicted and tombstoned, so the late sample is lost. The tests confirm this outcome.

issues.title: Txs ring only holds recent entries, so older commits are not tracked
issues.evidence: for i := uint32(0); i < s.txs.txIDCount; i++ {
issues.failure_scenario: If txs entries are cleaned up once their appends are older than the oldest open read, a late commit may already have been pruned. The comment's 'any in-memory sample' claim would then not hold. This depends on the isolation implementation, which is not shown.

units.headline: Add hasAppendIDAbove watermark check over series txs ring
units.reason: Core correctness guard for eviction races; it iterates the isolation ring and is a no-op when isolation is disabled.
focus: Ring iterator semantics: txIDCount and At()/Next() ordering and wraparound
Behavior when isolation is disabled
The ring may drop old entries, so the guard may miss them
